question: Why are prescribed and prohibited practices, including yogic limbs, said to be artificial here?
premises: In this scriptural context, everything prescribed is also, in another respect, prohibited.
Yogas consisting of limbs such as breath control fall within that same field.
Because they are constructed and rule-bound, they are artificial.
inference: Rule-based yogic practices are limited and artificial because they depend on injunction and prohibition rather than on the unconstructed reality.
uncertainties: The verse compresses a strong polemic; the exact scope of 'all' may be rhetorical within the cited scripture.
plain_english: Here, everything that is prescribed is also, in another way, prohibited. Yogas made up of limbs such as breath control would therefore be artificial, because they are constructed.
